pr.title: Review the pull requests that request the operator's review
pr.head: 487ceaf2ede7f78b22a593a78d7f0795bcd0be6f

summary: The review loop (start-review-loop) reviews every new head of the pull requests it tracks. Its watcher script, watch-prs.sh, polls GitHub and reads a tracked file, one owner/repo#number per line, that sets which pull requests the loop watches. With --author, the watcher adopts pull requests: each cycle it appends the operator's open pull requests to the tracked file, and the loop reviews each new one.

Before this change, a teammate who asked the operator for a review got no review until someone added the pull request to the tracked file by hand. This change adds --review-requested <login>, which adopts each open pull request that requests that login by name. The request can come from the author, a CODEOWNERS rule, or a bot. A request to a team the login belongs to does not count, because CODEOWNERS can request a team on nearly every pull request. Adoption only appends, so the pull request stays tracked after the operator answers the request.

A requested pull request belongs to someone else. So review-pr reviews it in the cross-author mode: it posts REQUEST_CHANGES when it finds problems and a COMMENT when the head is clean, and it never changes the pull request's draft state.

The watcher's RESPONDED event asks for a re-review when the author answers without a push, by replying on a finding or resolving every thread. For a draft, it fires only on a pull request by the --author login, because a review never changes another author's draft state. For another author's pull request, it fires when the newest Projector verdict on the current head requests changes. The watcher reads that verdict from the marker in the review body, because GitHub's reviewDecision field stays null unless the base branch requires reviews.

cards.html:

  • Head 332f683: changes requested. Another author's answer without a push depended on reviewDecision, which GitHub leaves null without required reviews. Fixed at 487ceaf.
  • Head 487ceaf: clean, with both finding threads resolved. The gate passes: 847 tests, project check, and both plugin validations.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Operator: the GitHub account the loop runs for, which is the authenticated user.
  • Adopt: append a pull request to the tracked file so that the loop reviews it.
  • RESPONDED: a watcher event that asks for a re-review of an unchanged head after the author answers.

groups.title: The watcher adopts requested pull requests
groups.kicker: A second listing in watch-prs.sh feeds the same adoption loop
intro: The new listed function prints the numbers of open pull requests from up to two listings: the operator's own pull requests (--author) and those that request a login (--review-requested). adopt appends every number that the tracked file does not name yet, as before. Each listing fails on its own, so if one listing fails, the other still adopts in that cycle.

The search uses GitHub's user-review-requested: qualifier rather than review-requested:, because review-requested: also matches requests to the login's teams. The watcher checks the login against GitHub's login characters before it builds the query, so a space cannot add a search term.

A row from GitHub now ends with the pull request author's login. In place of reviewDecision, the row carries the verdict: the newest Projector verdict whose marker names the current head, or - when there is none. In a public repository, only an owner, a member, or a collaborator can give a verdict, which matches project review status. When --author is set, the watcher reads a draft as waiting for sign-off only when that login wrote it. Another author's pull request waits when its verdict is changes-requested.

files.note: Adds the flag, the login check, and the listed function that feeds adopt. Reads the head's Projector verdict to decide when another author's pull request waits on a re-review.

checks.text: At b7c5460, one --once pass against kubernetes/kubernetes, with temporary tracked and state files, adopted the same 11 pull requests that gh pr list --search "user-review-requested:<login>" lists. The listing code has not changed since then.

On a public repository, a CODEOWNERS rule that names the operator brings fork pull requests from outsiders into the loop. setup refuses to run their code, but the loop still reviews and summarizes them.
Run read-only against this pull request, this head's PR_QUERY and PR_JQ print - for the current head and changes-requested for 332f683 and b7c5460. That matches the review markers on GitHub.
With a null reviewDecision and a changes-requested verdict, a fake-gh run prints RESPONDED once when a teammate replies on a finding, for both a draft and a ready pull request.

groups.title: The loop passes the flag and describes the wider scope
groups.kicker: start-review-loop, review-pr, and the plugin guide
intro: start-review-loop now passes --review-requested <operator> beside --author. When the loop starts, it also lists the requested pull requests. When it adopts a watcher that is already running, it checks for both flags. review-pr and docs/plugins.md describe the operator as the account that the loop tracks pull requests for, which includes the ones that request the operator's review.

checks.text: A watcher that started before this change has no --review-requested. The new check for both flags makes the loop restart it.

files.note: Widens the loop's scope and adds the flag to the startup listing, the first pass, and the check on a running watcher.

checks.text: This listing must match what the watcher adopts, because each head that the loop finds unreviewed must come back as NEW PR in the first pass.

files.note: Redefines the operator as the account the loop tracks pull requests for.

groups.title: Tests drive the watcher through a fake gh
groups.kicker: The fake gh answers the new search, and one test covers adoption
intro: The fake gh in tests/test_watchers.py now answers --search user-review-requested:<login> from each fixture's reviewRequests. The new test adopts only the open pull request that requests the operator. It also checks that the pull request stays tracked and reports NEW HEAD after the request is gone. The flag test adds --repo without an adoption flag, and a login that contains a space.

test_only_the_authors_own_draft_waits_on_a_clean_review runs the operator's draft and a teammate's requested draft through the same fix cycle. Only the operator's draft gets RESPONDED once the finding is resolved and the change request is dismissed.

The fake gh now serves review nodes that carry a verdict marker, and a repository's visibility. test_another_authors_answer_without_a_push_asks_for_a_re_review covers a draft, a ready pull request, a passerby's marker in a public repository, and a private repository. test_a_review_that_settles_findings_before_it_publishes_is_no_answer checks that a verdict on an earlier head does not count.
